 Advertisement Halloween forecast: Check out the trick-or-treat index
 Will your kids need an extra jacket or rain gear for trick or treating? Here is our latest forecast for Saturday. 
 By Jonathan Erdman • 3 hours ago Updated: October 30, 2026, 3:12 pm EDT Published: October 30, 2026, 10:00 am EDT Share Share
 1 . National overview Chevron Down 
 Halloween weather is forecast to be wet in some parts of the country, but looks either warm or dry for most others as parents get ready to shepherd their kids around their neighborhoods Saturday.
 Fortunately, we don't have a major storm in the forecast Saturday. But there may be weather headaches for some.
 National overview
 The map below shows where trick-or-treat weather Saturday evening is generally expected to be good (green dots), may have at least some weather annoyances to deal with (yellow dots) or could require rain gear or at least a warmer costume (red dots).

 Let's go into the trick-or-treat weather forecast region by region.
 ( MORE: How to keep Halloween fun without scaring your pet )
 Get More of Our News on Google

 Northeast nice ⭐
 High pressure will be in control, so we're not expecting any rain or snow. Temperatures should be pleasant by end of October standards and winds shouldn't be a problem.
 The kids will probably need a warmer costume or jacket if trick-or-treating extends after sunset, especially in New England. But other than that, don't worry about the weather Saturday evening in the Northeast.
 ( FORECAST DETAILS: Boston | D.C. | New York | Philly | Pittsburgh )
 South concerns? 🌧️
 While there is not a major storm on the weather map, there is a threat of scattered showers and thunderstorms in parts of the South Saturday evening.
 The forecast for this region has improved as the week has gone on, but there is still a chance of wet weather generally centered on the lower Mississippi Valley.
 So, consider carrying an umbrella with you just in case in these areas Saturday evening.
 ( FORECAST DETAILS: Atlanta | Dallas | Houston | Miami | Nashville ) 
 Midwest warm, but wet? 🌧️
 You couldn't ask for more pleasant temperatures for Halloween, with evening 50s or 60s in most areas. Winds won't be much of a headache either.
 But there is a threat of showers, possibly a rumble of thunder, especially from parts of the Plains of Nebraska and Kansas into the Lower Ohio Valley.
 Light, short-lived showers are also possible in parts of Dakotas, Minnesota, Wisconsin and the upper Peninsula of Michigan. 
 So you may want to have some umbrellas or rain jackets along for the trick-or-treat walk through the neighborhood in areas shaded green on the map below.
 ( FORECAST DETAILS: Chicago | Cleveland | Detroit | Kansas City ) 
 West wet, again 🌧️
 Unfortunately, parts of the West may have less than ideal weather Saturday evening.
 Parts of California, Nevada, Oregon and Arizona could have rain to contend with. Again, the areas with the best chance of rain are shown in darker green in the map below. Consider bringing at least umbrellas and rain jackets for trick-or-treating in those areas.
 And in parts of the Sierra Nevada, that could fall as snow.
 The clouds and precipitation will also hold temperatures a bit cooler than usual for Halloween in most areas, including areas not shown in green below.
 So, particularly in the Northwest, even if there is not any rain or snow, you may want to choose a warmer Halloween costume for your kids this year.
 Incidentally, it appears likely San Diego will have its first measurable rain on Halloween in 39 years . 
 ( FORECAST DETAILS: Denver | Las Vegas | L.A. | Phoenix | Seattle )
